name: External validation on the Hannousse and Yahiouche web page phishing dataset
status: frozen before any external evaluation was run

dataset.title: Web page phishing detection
dataset.paper: Hannousse, A. and Yahiouche, S. (2021). Towards benchmark datasets for machine learning based website phishing detection: An experimental study. Engineering Applications of Artificial Intelligence, 104, 104347.
dataset.changes: Only the url and status columns are used; the 87 published features are ignored. Rows are filtered and deduplicated as described under preparation.

models.source: the frozen benchmark models in artifacts/benchmark/models.pkl, trained by scripts/train_benchmark.py on the 24 PhiUSIIL training examples
models.quantum_kernel: exact statevector simulation between each external example and the 24 training examples; no QPU
models.scaler: configs/feature-scaler.json, unchanged; values outside the training range are clipped and counted
models.decision_rule: each model's default predict; no threshold, calibration, or retraining

preparation.rule: derive the host from url with src.inference.predictor.extract_host, which also applies normalize_host (lowercase, drop port and trailing dot, strip one leading www.); exclude rows it rejects
group rows by registrable domain with src.data.benchmark_split.group_key; exclude every group whose rows carry both labels
exclude every group that also occurs among the registrable domains of any row of the PhiUSIIL snapshot, so no external domain was available to the benchmark
keep the first row of each remaining group in file order; exclude the rest

primary_set: the rows remaining after all four preparation steps

confidence_intervals.method: percentile bootstrap over rows of the primary set

reporting: Publish all four models regardless of their results.
Report the count excluded by each preparation step, the class counts of the primary set, and how many values each feature clipped.
Publish no host or URL; the published file holds only aggregates.
Label the quantum-kernel SVM as exact simulation; this validation runs no hardware jobs.
Nothing in the benchmark or in this file changes after the external results are seen.
